import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 426

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/426](https://www.erdosproblems.com/426)
- [Er76b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Proceedings of the Fifth British Combinatorial Conference (1976), 169-192.
- [EnEr72] Entringer, R. C. and Erdős, Paul, *On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1972), 112-115.
- [HaSc73] Harary, Frank and Schwenk, Allen J., *On the number of unique subgraphs*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1973), 156-160.
- [Br75] Brouwer, A. E., *Note: "On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph"
  (J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B 13 (1972), 112-115) by R. C. Entringer and P. Erdős*.
  J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B (1975), 184-185.
- [BrCh24] Bradač, D. and Christoph, M., *Unique subgraphs are rare*. arXiv:2410.16233 (2024).
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos426

/-- Sanity check: the empty graph `⊥` is a unique subgraph of itself. Its only subgraph is `⊥`
(everything `≤ ⊥` equals `⊥`), which is isomorphic to `⊥` via the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUniqueSubgraph_bot_bot {V : Type*} : IsUniqueSubgraph (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) ⊥ := by
  refine ⟨⊥, ⟨le_refl _, ⟨Iso.refl⟩⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro G' ⟨hle, -⟩
  exact le_bot_iff.mp hle

/--
We say $H$ is a unique subgraph of $G$ if there is exactly one way to find $H$ as a subgraph
(not necessarily induced) of $G$. Is there a graph on $n$ vertices with
$$\gg \frac{2^{\binom{n}{2}}}{n!}$$
many distinct unique subgraphs?

Bradač and Christoph [BrCh24] have proved the answer is no: if $f(n)$ is the maximum number of
unique subgraphs in a graph on $n$ vertices then
$$f(n) = o\left(\frac{2^{\binom{n}{2}}}{n!}\right).$$

The $\gg$ below is read as: some constant $c>0$ works for arbitrarily large $n$. The negation
of the proposition on the right is then exactly $f(n) = o(2^{\binom{n}{2}}/n!)$, the form in
which Bradač and Christoph [BrCh24] resolved the problem.

The linked file states the resolution in that negated form, as
`Tendsto fSeq atTop (nhds 0)`. It counts the isomorphism classes occurring as unique subgraphs,
whereas `uniqueSubgraphCount` counts their representatives $G\leq H$; uniqueness forces exactly
one representative per class, so the two counts agree.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos426.lean"]
theorem erdos_426 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ n.choose 2 / n.factorial) ≤ (uniqueSubgraphCount H : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos426

findings.description: The [Br75] bibliography entry (lines 30–32) gives an erroneous Math Reviews title, beginning “Note: ‘On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph’ … by R. C. Entringer and P. Erdős”. Brouwer’s actual article is titled “On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph”. This is only a reference slip; neither Lean statement is affected.
findings.source_evidence: Brouwer’s own publication list, https://aeb.win.tue.nl/publ.html, lists the article in JCT (B) 18 (1975), 184–185 and explicitly says “MR (erroneously) gives the title as” the wording reproduced in the Lean file. The Eindhoven publication record and Crossref record for DOI 10.1016/0095-8956(75)90047-7 also give the actual title.
findings.suggested_fix: Change [Br75] to: Brouwer, A. E., “On the number of unique subgraphs of a graph”, J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. B 18 (1975), 184–185.

reformulations.difference: The theorem expresses the cited limit-zero resolution as a negative answer to a positive lower bound holding for arbitrarily large n. It counts unique subgraph representatives rather than the quotient classes counted in the linked formal proof.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Put D(n)=2^(n.choose 2)/n!, which is positive for every n. Negating the right-hand proposition gives: for every ε>0, eventually every n-vertex H satisfies uniqueSubgraphCount(H)/D(n)<ε. Since the graph type is finite and nonempty and these ratios are nonnegative, this is exactly convergence of their maximum to zero. Moreover, sending a counted representative to its isomorphism class is bijective: existence supplies a representative inside H, and uniqueness prevents two such representatives in the same class. In /workspace/review/bridge.lean I proved the exact ↔ between the file’s entire theorem statement and the linked definition’s `Tendsto fSeq atTop (nhds 0)`, without sorry or additional axioms. This matches Bradač–Christoph Theorem 1.2; it does not assert a general equivalence between frequent and eventual positive lower bounds.

reformulations.difference: The imported helpers count only spanning subgraphs, whereas Bradač–Christoph explicitly allow subgraphs on arbitrary subsets of the vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an n-vertex host H, let U(H) count all unique subgraphs and S(H) count the spanning ones. An ordinary n-vertex subgraph of H must be spanning, so 0≤U(H)−S(H)≤u(<n), where u(<n) counts all isomorphism classes of graphs on fewer than n vertices. The proof of Bradač–Christoph Lemma 2.1 explicitly states u(<n)=o(2^(n choose 2)/n!). This bound is uniform in H, so the maxima of U and S differ by at most that lower-order term. Their little-o conclusions, and hence the sourced resolution stated here, are equivalent. The counts themselves need not be equal at a fixed n.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization or stale status was found. Both declarations were checked. The empty-graph test is correct in the documented spanning convention. Scratch proofs establish count(⊥)=1, including n=0 and n=1, positivity of the denominator and finite counting sets; independent enumeration also checked graphs through n=5. The linked proof targets Lean/Mathlib 4.32. A scratch-only compatibility port compiled under 4.33.1 after two compatibility settings and two proof-only adjustments; `f_tendsto_zero` and the exact statement-equivalence proof both have only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] as axioms. The live Erdős page was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematics was checked against the cited primary paper and status corroborated by the current problem database. Full texts of Harary–Schwenk and Brouwer were unavailable; their metadata and Bradač–Christoph’s summaries were read. No declaration in this file separately states their historical lower bounds.
